title: Prioritization ladder for optimization requests: cost, latency, regression risk
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Enterprise customers submit non-bug advisory requests around inference optimizations (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). We lack a clear, repeatable prioritization method that balances financial impact, end-user latency, and regression risk to output quality. Current intake lanes are noisy, leading to long lead times for high-value enterprise asks.

Goal:
Define and operationalize a prioritization ladder that product and solutions teams can apply at intake to route optimization/advisory requests into: self-serve guidance, engineering triage, or a fast-track enterprise engagement with SLA and billing. The ladder should be automatable for the majority of cases (scoring based on telemetry + customer metadata) and provide a transparent override path for PMs and Sales.

Scope (what this ticket delivers):
- A four-tier prioritization ladder with clear quantitative thresholds: 1) Self-serve (docs + templates), 2) Low-touch advisory (SE hour), 3) Engineering work (sprint), 4) Enterprise fast-track (SLA + dedicated runbook).
- Scoring rubric combining estimated token-cost saving, observed p99 latency delta, and regression risk score from our eval harness.
- Intake form additions (required fields) and mapping rules to auto-score requests in the console intake flow and CRM webhook.
- Hand-off playbook for fast-track: SLA terms, billing trigger, kickoff checklist, and stakeholder RACI.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict numeric thresholds vs. flexible banding: we chose banding with explicit override reasons to reduce misclassification for niche enterprise workloads.
- Complexity of scoring inputs: prioritized using telemetry-derived metrics (cost & latency) and a conservative regression-risk proxy (eval failure rate + model-version-change flag) to avoid requiring manual eval submission for every customer.
- Automation vs. human review: automation will handle ~70% of intake; remaining are routed to a weekly triage for final decision.

Success metrics:
- Median time-to-assignment for enterprise-priority optimization requests reduced from 14 days to <=3 days.
- Percent of requests auto-classified correctly (as validated by triage) >= 75% after 6 weeks.
- First-pass solutions that meet target latency/cost improvements in >= 60% of fast-track engagements.

Artifacts / Links:
- Draft rubric & threshold spreadsheet: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Optimization+Prioritization+Ladder (internal)
- Intake form prototype (Console): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/opt-intake-proto
- Evaluation harness change PR (ENG): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/384
- Example SLA template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LEGAL/Optimization+Fast-Track+SLA

Open questions / blockers:
- Need final sign-off from Legal on SLA billing triggers (in review with legal@redwood.ai).
- Determines mapping of customer-reported business value field — Sales wants a free-text field; engineering needs structured tiers. Action: implement both, require tier selection for scoring and optional free-text for Sales context.
- Integrating regression-risk score into the console requires a small API from Evals team (ENG-4217). Engineering ETA: 2 sprints.

Next steps (immediate):
1) PM to finalize scoring bands with Eng/SE (due 2026-03-05).
2) Product design to ship intake form mockups and tooltips (design ticket planned).
3) Engineering to implement scoring endpoint (ENG-4217) and add webhook mapping to CRM.
4) Pilot with two enterprise accounts (account A and B) and measure auto-classification accuracy.

Notes on enterprise handling: for fast-track cases create a temporary dedicated Slack channel and require a 48h SLA for kickoff call. Add an opt-in billing clause that converts advisory hours into a reserved capacity commitment if the customer signs a 3-month optimization retainer.
